final_lessons: Awaiting feedback on whether high LR helps in low-step budgets.
Adam at moderate LR outperformed high-LR RMSprop; prefer Adam-family optimizers with reasonable LR in low-step budgets.
Adaptive optimizers (Adam/AdamW/RMSprop) with moderate LR reliably beat low-LR SGD/Adagrad under short step budgets.

Smaller d_model with moderate depth outperforms larger models on limited training budgets, suggesting regularization or parameter efficiency is critical.

The d_model 64, 2-layer configuration continues to be optimal, reinforcing that smaller architectures with adequate FFN capacity are best for this task and budget.
Adding depth to the d_model 64 configuration appears beneficial when FFN capacity remains high, suggesting depth helps when base model size is constrained.
Shallower models with d_model 64 outperform deeper variants, indicating that excess depth hurts generalization more than limited expressiveness on this budget.
When forced to choose among deeper models, d_model 64 with high FFN capacity still outperforms larger d_model configurations regardless of depth.
The smallest d_model option with high FFN capacity outperforms mid-size options, confirming that minimal d_model with compensatory FFN width is optimal for this constrained regime.
The d_model 64 single-layer config with moderate FFN is a top performer, confirming that minimal depth with small d_model wins in this regime.
